title: IMO confirms tanker JIF BARRACUDA damaged off Khor Fakkan
excerpt: The Netherlands-flagged tanker was hit northeast of Khor Fakkan on 18 October, injuring one seafarer, according to the IMO.
x_post: The IMO has confirmed the tanker JIF BARRACUDA was damaged northeast of Khor Fakkan on 18 October, with one seafarer injured. #MaritimeSecurity #Shipping #Seafarers #StraitOfHormuz
fact_check_fixes: INC-20261018-014: UKMTO warning 177-26 places the tug strike northeast of Khor Fakkan, not 'in the same area'.

notes: In the Black Sea paragraph say only that Russia's defence ministry claimed its Geran drones struck three dry cargo ships and a container ship in the Black Sea on 22 October carrying military cargo, with no names and no independent confirmation, and drop the sentence about a ship drifting off Giresun with a Turkish crew member, because that ship is the Palau-flagged Aroyat, struck off Novorossiysk on 27 September and reported by DHA on 22 October.

JIF BARRACUDA (IMO 9345506) is a Netherlands-flagged multi-purpose tug, not a tanker: her operator Jifmar and VesselFinder both give tug, so call her a tug in the headline, standfirst, lede, key points, paragraph and tweet, and do not attach a sea-mine claim to her, because the IRGC mine claims in the same sources are about other vessels.

The lead is an unverified claim, so say in the headline, key points and lede that the IRGC's seven-vessel claim is unconfirmed, that UKMTO has issued no warning matching it, and that President Trump accused Iran of faking the hits to push up oil prices, as gCaptain reported on 22 October.

In the Able paragraph say the Palau-flagged general cargo ship Able, damaged by a drone off Bulgaria on 6 October, later sank off the Turkish coast after her crew was taken off, as Sofia Globe reported on 20 October.
